transcript.text: Hi everyone. We've got fourteen 55-gallon drums of spent coolant from the machining area staged on spill pallets in the waste staging area, and the disposal vendor still hasn't received authorization. I need to get the round-robin review going so we can approve the disposal route and shipment controls. I'd like to get lab quality, waste logistics, and warehouse supervision involved to walk through the removal plan. Who's ready to start that review?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag something before we proceed with the disposal route. My laboratory analysis found 2.4% chlorinated solvent in the spent coolant. The site's waste matrix requires that any batch at or above 1.0% chlorinated solvent be sent to hazardous-liquid treatment rather than ordinary coolant recycling. I completed this analysis yesterday, but the result has not yet been attached to the waste authorization. We need to make sure the disposal route reflects this hazardous classification before Elena approves anything.

transcript.text: Before we finalize the shipment controls, I need to flag something from my end. I confirmed with the disposal contractor that their tanker permit allows a maximum of 8 of these drums per load, so the 14 drums will need to be split into two shipments — one load of 8 and a second load of 6. I received this permit condition in the contractor's service email but haven't yet entered it into the transport booking system, so we need to account for that split in the removal plan.

transcript.text: I need to flag something from my warehouse inspection before we finalize the removal plan. I found active seepage at the base of exactly 4 of the 14 drums. Those 4 drums must be placed in UN-rated overpacks before any movement. The other 10 drums are fine to remain on their existing spill pallets. I recorded this inspection on the shift clipboard, but I haven't yet updated the waste file, so this needs to be factored into the removal plan.
